instruction: Component Grid Array with Alternating Rotation The file `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\cell.dae` contains a single rectangular bar (500 x 100 x 100 mm) centered on the X-Y origin with its base at Z=0 (so it spans X in [-0.25, 0.25] m, Y in [-0.05, 0.05] m, Z in [0, 0.10] m). 1. Import `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\cell.dae` and promote the bar to a single reusable ComponentDefinition (or equivalent COLLADA `<library_geometries>` referenced by multiple `<node>` instances). 2. Create a 10 x 10 grid of 100 instances, one per (i, j) for i, j in 0..9. Each instance's local origin is placed at world position (i x 0.7, j x 0.7, 0) - the grid spacing is 700 mm. 3. Save the native SketchUp model to `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\answer.skp`. The DAE must reference a single shared geometry definition, not 100 independent copies of the mesh. Requirements: 1. `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\answer.skp` can be opened and inspected as a native SketchUp model. 2. Exactly one geometry definition is referenced (instanced 100 times). 3. All 100 expected cell centers are covered - for every (i, j) with i, j in 0..9, some vertex lies within 5 mm of (i*0.7, j*0.7). 4. For every cell, the world-space AABB of that cell's vertices matches the expected shape: - Even (i+j): X-span 500 mm, Y-span 100 mm, Z-span 100 mm (no rotation) - Odd (i+j): X-span 100 mm, Y-span 500 mm, Z-span 100 mm (90 deg about Z) within 5 mm of the expected extents.
